speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 88)
question: What state is born when agitation ceases?
premises: Having whirled, whirled, by body swiftly from falling.
By agitation-power ceasing: supreme is born state.
inference: Agitation's stopping is not collapse — the supreme state is born from it.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 89)
question: What power brings the form?
premises: On supports or by power, by knowing, from mind-dissolving.
Born power-penetration agitation-end: Bhairava form.
inference: Whichever of the three means ends in agitation-calm — Bhairava form is born.

speaker: Bhairava (declaring)
question: When is freedom born?
premises: Tradition this, O Goddess, hear — rightly I tell.
Even freedom is born at once, when eyes are unwinkingly fixed.
inference: Freedom is born at the very moment the gaze locks unwinkingly.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 90)
question: How does one enter brahma?
premises: Contraction of ears, at lower gate likewise and.
Unsmeared, unploughed, meditating: should enter brahman eternal.
inference: Ear-contraction plus the lower gate, meditating unsmeared, enters eternal brahman.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 91)
question: What dissolves from above the pit?
premises: At well or great pit, having stood above, looking.
Undivided mind rightly: at once mind-dissolving, plainly.
inference: Looking down from above the pit dissolves mind plainly.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 92)
question: Where is Śiva-state where mind goes?
premises: Where mind goes — outside, inside, or even.
There Śiva-state: by pervasiveness, where will it go?
inference: Mind cannot exit pervasiveness — wherever it goes, Śiva-state already is.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 93)
question: What is manifested on the eye-road?
premises: Where eye-road: consciousness manifested of the pervader.
From only-that-natured, cit-dissolving: full-self-ness.
inference: On every eye-road, consciousness only; dissolving in cit, full-self-ness.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 94)
question: Which states fill with reality?
premises: At hunger-end, fear, grief, abyss, battle-fled.
At curiosity-thirst end: reality-being-full state.
inference: Even the passions' ends are reality-full states when met thus.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 95)
question: Where does mind leave and the lord spread?
premises: In things remembered, seen: mind should leave in place.
Own body unsupported made: spreads forth lord.
inference: Leaving mind in the seen thing, the unsupported lord spreads forth.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 96)
question: How does the gaze withdraw?
premises: Anywhere on thing placed: slowly gaze withdraw.
That knowing with mind: O Goddess, void-abode may be.
inference: Slow withdrawal leaves mind-knowing abiding in void.
